A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Enol content is maximum in
A.sol_text:
The structure shown in option (3) is:

(benzene ring)–C(=O) ⇌ (benzene ring)–C(=OH) with a double bond in the ring

Enol content is maximum in aromatic ketones because:
- The enol form is stabilized by resonance with the aromatic ring
- The aromatic system can delocalize the negative charge that develops during enolization
- This resonance stabilization makes the enol form more stable compared to aliphatic ketones
- In option (1): Ph₂CH–CHO has only one carbonyl, less stabilization
- In option (2): The diketone has competing enol forms but lacks aromatic stabilization
- In option (4): The ester group withdraws electron density, reducing enol stability

Therefore, the aromatic ketone in option (3) has the maximum enol content due to resonance stabilization by the benzene ring.

A.text:
A, B, C and D are the points of intersection of a circle and a rectangular hyperbola which have different centres. If AB passes through the centre of the hyperbola. Then CD passes through the
(1) Centre of the hyperbola
(2) Centre of the circle
(3) Mid-points of the centres of the circle and hyperbola
(4) Focus of hyperbola
options: Mid-points of the centres of the circle and hyperbola
A.sol_text:
Answer : (2)
Solution:
If the centres of the circle and the hyperbola be (α, β) and (h, k), respectively and the points are A(x₁, y₁), B(x₂, y₂), C(x₃, y₃) and D(x₄, y₄) then
h + α = (x₁ + x₂ + x₃ + x₄)/2 and
k + β = (y₁ + y₂ + y₃ + y₄)/2 ...(1)
where (h,k) lies on AB, then chords of the hyperbola, passing its centre, are bisected at the centre.
h = (x₁ + x₂)/2, k = (y₁ + y₂)/2 ...(2)
Then (1) and (2)
α = (x₃ + x₄)/2, β = (y₃ + y₄)/2
⇒ (α, β) is the mid-point of CD and lies on CD.

A.text: P and Q are points on ellipse (x²/a²) + (y²/b²) = 1 whose centre is C. The eccentric angle of P and Q differ by a right angle. If angle PCQ is minimum, then the eccentric angle of P can be
A.sol_text:
Since eccentric angle of P and Q differ by a right angle, we can take P(a cos θ, b sin θ) and Q(−a sin θ, b cos θ)
Slope of CP = (b sin θ)/(a cos θ)
Slope of CQ = (−b cos θ)/(a sin θ)
If α is the angle between CP and CQ,
tan α = |(b sin θ)/(a cos θ) + (b cos θ)/(a sin θ)|/|1 − (b² sin θ cos θ)/(a² cos θ sin θ)|
⇒ α = tan⁻¹(2ab/((a² − b²)·sin² θ))
α is minimum, if sin² θ is maximum.
i.e., 2θ = π/2 ⇒ θ = π/4

A.text: While calculating mean and standard deviation of six observations a student has taken an observation 9 in place of 6 by mistake and calculated the mean and standard deviation as 7 and 1 respectively. Then the correct standard deviation is
A.sol_text:
Answer : (2)
Hint:
σ = √((Σx_i²)/N - (x̄)²)

Solution:
Incorrect x̄ = 7
⇒ Incorrect Σx_i = 7 × 6 = 42
So correct Σx_i = 42 − 9 + 6 = 39
⇒ correct x̄ = 39/6 = 13/2
Incorrect σ = 1
√((Incorrect Σx_i²)/6 − (7)²) = 1
Incorrect Σx_i² = 300
So correct
σ = √((correct Σx_i²)/6 − (correct x̄)²)
= √(255/6 − (13/2)²) = 0.5

A.text: Let P be a point in first quadrant on ellipse (x²/256) + (y²/81) = 1 such that the length of intercept between the coordinate axes on the tangent to the ellipse at P is of minimum length. The area of triangle formed by the tangent at P and the coordinate axes is
A.sol_text:
Let the point P be (16 cos θ, 9 sin θ)

Equation of tangent: (x/16) cos θ + (y/9) sin θ = 1

If it cut the x and y-axis respectively at Q and R
then Q ≡ (16 sec θ, 0) & R ≡ (0, 9 cosec θ)

(QR)² = 256 sec² θ + 81 cosec² θ
= 256 + 81 + 256 tan² θ + 81 cot²θ

Now, (256tan²θ + 81cot²θ)/2 ≥ (256 · tan²θ · 81 · cot²θ)^(1/2)
⇒ 256 tan² θ + 81 cot² θ ≥ 288

and equality holds for 256 tan² θ = 81 cot²θ
⇒ tan⁴θ = 81/256 ⇒ tan θ = 3/4

Area of △OQR = (1/2) · 16 · sec θ · 9 cosec θ = (1/2) · 16 · (5/4) · 9 · (5/3)
= 150 sq. units

B.text: The vertices B and C of △ABC lie on the line 3y = 4x and positive x-axis respectively and the side BC passes through the point (2/3, 2/3). If ABOC is a rhombus, O being the origin and coordinates of vertex A is (α, β) then value of 5(α + β) is equal to
B.sol_text:
Let OC = a
OC = CA = AB = BO

Let B = (x₁, (4/3)x₁)

A = (a + x₁, (4/3)x₁)

Equation of BC is y = ((4/3)x₁)/(x₁ - a) (x - a)

∴ x₁ = (3/5) ⇒ a = 1

∴ A = (8/5, 4/5) = (α, β)

∴ 5(α + β) = 12

B.text: Let the radius of the circle which passes through the point (1, 1) and which touches the circle x² + y² + 4x - 6y - 3 = 0 at the point (2, 3) on it is r. Then 2r is equal to_______.
B.sol_text:
Answer: 05.00
Solution:

Equation of the required circle is
(x² + y² + 4x - 6y - 3) + λ((x - 2)² + (y - 3)²) = 0 ...(1)
Put x = 1, y = 1
(1 + 1 + 4 - 6 - 3) + λ(1 + 4) = 2
λ = (3/5)

Put λ = (3/5) in equation (1)
Equation of the required circle is
(x² + y² + 4x - 6y - 3) + (3/5)((x - 2)² + (y - 3)²) = 0
5x² + 5y² + 20x - 30y - 15 + 3x² + 3y² - 12x - 18y + 39 = 0
8x² + 8y² + 8x - 48y + 24 = 0
x² + y² + x - 6y + 3 = 0

r = √((1/4) + 9 - 3) = √(25/4) = (5/2)
2r = 5.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: The number of integral values of parameter 'a' for which three chords of the ellipse x²/(2a²) + y²/a² = 1 (other than its diameter) passing through the point P(11a, -a²/4) are bisected by the parabola y² = 4ax, is
B.sol_text:
Any point on the parabola y² = 4ax is (at², 2at). Equation of chord of the ellipse x²/(2a²) + y²/a² = 1, whose mid-point is (at², 2at) is x·at²/(2a²) + y·2at/a² = a²t²/(2a²) + 4a²t²/a² = a²t²/(2a²) + 4a²t²/a²

As it passes through (11a, -a²/4),
⇒ 11at - 4(a²/4) = at³ + 8at
⇒ at³ - 3at + a² = 0
⇒ t³ - 3t + a = 0 (a ≠ 0)

Now, three chords of the ellipse will be bisected by the parabola if the equation has three real and distinct roots.

Let f(t) = t³ - 3t + a
f'(t) = 3t² - 3 = 0 ⇒ t = ±1

So, f(1)·f(-1) < 0
⇒ a ∈ (-2, 2)

But a ≠ 0, so a ∈ (-2, 0) ∪ (0, 2)
∴ Number of integral values of 'a' = 2.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
